newsitem.title: USA: Weather-related cattle deaths reported in Nebraska.
newsitem.headline: Weather-related cattle deaths reported in Nebraska.

text.p: Three to five percent of feedlot cattle in northeast Nebraska have died during the last month of severe winter weather, according to the Nebraska Cattleman Association, based in Lincoln, Neb.
"That part of the state has been hammered hard since the last half of December and the better part of this month, and they're getting pretty tired of it," said Ken Fox, market analyst with the group.
Fox estimated about 250,000 head of cattle on feed were affected by the severe weather.
Currently, there are about two million head of cattle on feed overall in Nebraska, said Jeff Stolle, vice president of marketing with the association.
"We've heard estimates of anywhere from three to five percent death loss, including calls of 3,000 head feedlots reporting 150 dead," Fox said.
"The cattle don't want to move because its too damn cold to do anything," Fox said.
Fox said it was extremely difficult getting an accurate head count because of the large number of small operations in that area that had not been contacted.
Northeastern Nebraska has a high concentration of feedlots that range from small farmer-feeder lots to large commercial operations, he noted.

The rest of the state's feedlots were reporting less problems outside of slow weight gains because other areas have not been hit as hard for as long as the corner bordering South Dakota and Iowa, Fox said.
